words.en: A sneaker is a type of soft shoe that you wear for sports or as informal wear.

words.ex: The clown walked on a tightrope above the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 小丑在人群上方的钢丝上行走。
words.en: A tightrope is a tightly stretched wire or rope fixed high above the ground, on which acrobats perform feats.

words.tr:
n. 崇拜；崇敬；礼拜；
v. 崇拜；尊崇；做礼拜；
words.ex: The ancient people showed worship to the sun.
words.ex_cn: 古人对太阳进行崇拜。
words.en: The feeling or expression of reverence and adoration for a deity.

chapters.name: Unit 5 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: He decided to drop out of the competition.
words.ex_cn: 他决定不参加比赛。
words.en: If someone drops out of a school or a course, they leave it before they have finished it.

words.tr: phrase. 跟随某人的领导；照某人的做法去做
words.ex: He decided to follow his friend's lead and study engineering.
words.ex_cn: 他决定跟随朋友的脚步，学习工程。
words.en: To follow someone's lead means to do as they do or to follow their example in a particular situation.

words.tr: phrase. v. 给予，奉献（时间、精力等）
words.ex: He likes to give of his time to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢付出自己的时间去帮助别人。
words.en: To offer or provide something, often in a generous or selfless manner.

words.tr: 短语动词. 无私地奉献自己；付出自己的时间、精力或情感帮助他人
words.ex: He always gives of himself to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他总是无私地帮助别人。
words.en: To devote oneself to a task or to helping others.

words.tr: phrase. 奉献自己的时间；自愿付出时间帮助他人
words.ex: He gives of his time to help old people at the community center.
words.ex_cn: 他在社区中心花时间帮助老人。
words.en: To willingly spend one's time doing something, especially to help others.

words.tr: 短语动词. 捐赠自己的钱；慷慨解囊
words.ex: He gives of his money to help poor people.
words.ex_cn: 他捐出自己的钱来帮助穷人。
words.en: To donate or contribute money generously.

words.tr: abbr. 诸如此类；等等；“et cetera”的缩写
words.ex: I bought apples, bananas, etc.
words.ex_cn: 我买了苹果、香蕉等。
words.en: Used at the end of a list to indicate that further, similar items are included.

words.tr: phrase. 气得发疯；大动肝火；惊慌失措
words.ex: My mom will have a fit if she sees my messy room.
words.ex_cn: 如果我妈妈看到我乱糟糟的房间，她会大发脾气的。
words.en: To become very angry or upset about something.

words.ex: I look up to my teacher because she is kind and smart.
words.ex_cn: 我尊敬我的老师，因为她善良又聪明。
words.en: If you look up to someone, you respect and admire them.

words.tr: phrase. 达到（标准）；符合（期望）；比得上
words.ex: He cannot measure up to his brother's standards.
words.ex_cn: 他达不到他哥哥的标准。
words.en: To reach the standard that is needed or expected.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人奉若神明；极度崇拜某人；把某人理想化
words.ex: People often put famous stars on a pedestal.
words.ex_cn: 人们常常把明星捧得很高。
words.en: To admire someone so much that you believe they can do no wrong.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人奉若神明；极度崇拜某人；把某人置于高不可攀的地位
words.ex: People often put famous stars upon a pedestal.
words.ex_cn: 人们常常把明星捧得很高。
words.en: To admire or respect someone greatly, often to the point of considering them perfect or incapable of doing wrong.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人奉若神明；把某人置于高不可攀的地位；极度崇拜某人
words.ex: People often place celebrities on a pedestal.
words.ex_cn: 人们常常把名人捧得很高。
words.en: To admire or worship someone greatly, often to the point of overlooking their faults.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人奉为偶像；把某人捧上神坛；过分崇拜某人
words.ex: He placed his father upon a pedestal.
words.ex_cn: 他把父亲奉为偶像。
words.en: To admire or treat someone with excessive reverence or idealization.

words.tr: phrase. 把……做得过火；把……推向极端
words.ex: He took the joke too far and made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他把玩笑开得太过分了，让她哭了。
words.en: To carry something to an extreme or excessive degree.

words.tr: phrase. v. 走得太远；做得过分
words.ex: He went too far when he broke his sister's toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他弄坏他妹妹的玩具时，他做得太过分了。
words.en: To go beyond what is reasonable or acceptable.

words.tr: phrase. 代替某人；取代某人
words.ex: He will take the place of someone who left the company.
words.ex_cn: 他将接替离开公司的人。
words.en: To substitute or replace someone in a particular role or position.

words.tr: phrase. 代替某人；接替某人的位置
words.ex: He will take someone's place in the team next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下个星期将代替某个人加入团队。
words.en: To take someone's place means to do something instead of them, especially because they are unable to do it or because they have stopped doing it.

words.tr: phrase. 但凡你想得起的；不管什么
words.ex: We have apples, bananas, you name it.
words.ex_cn: 我们有苹果、香蕉，等等所有东西。
words.en: You use 'you name it' to indicate that a list of things could be extended indefinitely because there are so many possibilities.

chapters.name: Unit 5 PASSAGE Ⅰ New Words

words.ex: The boxing match took place in an arena.
words.ex_cn: 拳击比赛在竞技场举行。
words.en: An arena is a place or scene of activity, debate, or conflict, especially one where a competition or performance is held.

words.ex: The plants grew artificially under blue lights.
words.ex_cn: 这些植物在蓝光下人工生长。
words.en: In a way that is made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.tr: n. 体育运动；田径运动；竞技；
words.ex: He loves athletics and runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱体育运动，每天早上跑步。
words.en: Athletics refers to sports in general, especially those that involve physical strength, speed, or endurance, such as running, jumping, and throwing.

words.tr: n. 律师；辩护律师；代理人
words.ex: The attorney helped the man with his case.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助那个人处理了他的案件。
words.en: An attorney is a lawyer who is qualified to represent a client in court.

words.ex: She blesses her children every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上为孩子们祝福。
words.en: If someone is blessed with a particular good quality or skill, they have that good quality or skill.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；骄傲自大的
words.ex: He is conceited because he thinks he is the smartest.
words.ex_cn: 他自以为是，因为他觉得自己最聪明。
words.en: If you say that someone is conceited, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they are far too proud of their abilities or achievements.

words.ex: The courageous firefighter saved the child from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的消防员从着火的房子里救出了孩子。
words.en: Someone who is courageous shows courage.

words.ex: The heat made the metal deform.
words.ex_cn: 热量使金属变形。
words.en: To deform something means to change its shape, usually in a way that makes it less attractive or useful.

words.tr: adj. 处于不利地位的；贫困的； v. “disadvantage”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The school helps disadvantaged children with free meals.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校为处境不利的孩子提供免费餐食。
words.en: People who are disadvantaged do not have the same opportunities or advantages as other people, often because of their financial situation or social position.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.ex: He checked his eligibility for the scholarship.
words.ex_cn: 他检查了自己是否有资格获得这笔奖学金。
words.en: The state of having the right to do or obtain something through satisfaction of the appropriate conditions.

words.ex: He became famous for his music and gained great fame.
words.ex_cn: 他因音乐而闻名，获得了巨大的名声。
words.en: the state of being known or talked about by many people, especially on account of notable achievements

words.tr:
v. 奉承；讨好
adj. 更平坦的；更扁平的；“flat”的比较级
adv. 更平直地；更直截了当地；“flat”的比较级
words.ex: He flatters his boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that may be sincere or may be intended to persuade you to do something.

words.ex: He fundamentally disagrees with the policy.
words.ex_cn: 他根本上不同意这项政策。
words.en: In a basic and important way; essentially.

words.tr: adv. 光荣地，辉煌地; 堂堂皇皇
words.ex: The sun rose gloriously over the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在山峦间辉煌地升起。
words.en: In a way that deserves or brings great fame and admiration.

words.tr: n. 重量级选手；体重超过平均水平的人；有影响力的人或事
words.ex: He is a heavyweight boxer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名重量级拳击手。
words.en: A heavyweight is a person or thing that is of great importance or influence, especially in a particular field or area.

words.tr: adj. 不屈不挠的；百折不挠的
words.ex: He is indomitable in facing challenges.
words.ex_cn: 他在面对挑战时永不言败。
words.en: If you say that someone has an indomitable spirit, you admire them because they never give up or admit that they have been defeated.

words.ex: He will inevitably fail if he doesn't study.
words.ex_cn: 如果他不学习，他不可避免地会失败。
words.en: If something will inevitably happen, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: He is invariably late for meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他总是开会迟到。
words.en: If something invariably happens or is invariably true, it always happens or is always true.

words.tr: adj. 合法的；法律认可的；合理的；
words.ex: This contract is legitimate and signed by both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同是合法的，并由双方签署。
words.en: Something that is legitimate is acceptable according to the law.

words.ex: He legitimately won the prize by following all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他通过遵守所有规则正当地赢得了奖品。
words.en: In a manner that is conforming to the law or to rules.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.tr: adj. 错误的； v. “misguide”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: His misguided decision cost him his job.
words.ex_cn: 他错误的决定让他丢了工作。
words.en: If you describe an opinion or plan as misguided, you are critical of it because you think it is based on an incorrect idea or judgment.

words.ex: He bought a new phone, but it was needless.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一部新手机，但这是不必要的。
words.en: If you describe something as needless, you mean that it is unnecessary and often harmful or undesirable.

words.ex: He overprotects his little sister by not letting her go outside alone.
words.ex_cn: 他不让她独自外出，对她太过保护。
words.en: To protect someone, especially a child, too much so that they do not learn to do things for themselves.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.ex: He works as a pipefitter in a factory.
words.ex_cn: 他在工厂里做管道工。
words.en: A pipefitter is a tradesperson who installs and maintains piping systems that carry liquids and gases.

words.ex: Going first is a privilege, not a right.
words.ex_cn: 优先权是一种特权，而不是权利。
words.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

words.tr: adj. 有特权的； v. “privilege”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a privileged student who gets free books.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有特权的学生，能免费获得书籍。
words.en: Having special rights, advantages, or immunities.

words.ex: He eats a grape every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一颗葡萄。
words.en: A grape is a small, round fruit that grows in bunches on a vine. Grapes can be green, red, or purple and are used for making wine, eating fresh, or drying into raisins.

words.tr: n. 推理；推论； v. “reason”的现在分词；
words.ex: His reasoning helped solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他的推理帮助解决了这个谜题。
words.en: the process of thinking about something in a logical way in order to form a conclusion or judgment

words.ex: He rightfully won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他理所当然地赢得了奖品。
words.en: In a manner that is in accordance with what is just, legal, or deserved.

words.ex: Her selflessness was evident in the way she always put others' needs before her own.
words.ex_cn: 她总是把别人的需要放在自己的前面，这充分体现了她的无私。
words.en: Selflessness is the quality of caring more about other people's needs and interests than about your own.

words.ex: He learned about sexual health in school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校学习了性健康。
words.en: Relating to the instincts, physiological processes, and activities connected with physical attraction or intimate physical contact between individuals.

words.ex: The knight held up his shield to block the arrow.
words.ex_cn: 骑士举起盾牌来挡箭。
words.en: A shield is a piece of armor held in the hand or worn on the arm to protect the body from missiles or blows. It can also refer to something that protects or defends someone or something from harm or danger.

words.tr: adj. 遍及全州的; 遍及全州地
words.ex: The law applies statewide.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律适用于全州。
words.en: extending throughout an entire state

words.ex: His status in the company is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司里的地位很高。
words.en: The status of someone or something is their position or situation according to the law or according to other people's opinions.

words.ex: He is a talented singer.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有才能的歌手。
words.en: Someone who is talented has a natural ability to do something well.

words.ex: Thankfully, the rain stopped before we left.
words.ex_cn: 幸亏雨在我们出发前停了。
words.en: In a way that expresses gratitude or relief.

words.tr:
adj. 惊险的； 令人激动的
v. 激动；震颤；兴奋；“thrill”的现在分词
words.ex: The roller coaster ride was thrilling.
words.ex_cn: 过山车之旅令人激动。
words.en: If something is thrilling, it causes a sudden feeling of great excitement, enjoyment, or sometimes fear.

words.tr: adj. 前所未闻的；空前的
words.ex: It was unheard-of for someone so young to achieve such success.
words.ex_cn: 对于如此年轻的人来说，取得这样的成功是前所未闻的。
words.en: If you describe something as unheard-of, you are emphasizing that it is very unusual and has never happened before.

words.tr: adj. 寻常的；不值得注意的
words.ex: The landscape was unremarkable, just a stretch of flat fields.
words.ex_cn: 这片风景很平凡，只是一片平坦的田野。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unremarkable, you mean that they are very ordinary, without many exciting, original, or attractive qualities.

words.tr:
v. 见证；
n. 证人；目击者；
words.ex: He witnessed the accident yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天目睹了那起事故。
words.en: A witness is someone who sees an event happen, especially a crime or an accident. Witnesses are often called upon to give evidence in court.

chapters.name: Unit 5 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: He likes apples, bananas, and the like.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢苹果、香蕉之类的水果。
words.en: used at the end of a list to indicate that there are other similar things or people that could also be included

words.ex: You must look to your health before it's too late.
words.ex_cn: 你必须注意你的健康，趁还来得及。
words.en: To expect or depend on someone or something to do something or provide something.

words.tr: phrase. 拿某人作比较；以某标准衡量某人
words.ex: Don't measure yourself against others; just do your best.
words.ex_cn: 不要拿自己和别人比较；尽力就好。
words.en: To compare someone's abilities, achievements, or qualities with those of another person.

words.tr: phrase. 用…来衡量某事物；以…为标准评估某事物
words.ex: We can measure something against a standard to see if it is good.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以用一个标准来衡量某物，看看它是否好。
words.en: To compare something with something else in order to judge its value, importance, etc.

words.tr: phrase. 在表面上；从表面看；外表上
words.ex: On the surface, the plan looks simple.
words.ex_cn: 表面上看，这个计划很简单。
words.en: Superficially or at first glance; appearing to be true without deeper examination.

words.tr: phrase. 在...之上；加之；紧接着
words.ex: The book is on top of the table.
words.ex_cn: 书在桌子上面。
words.en: In addition to; in control of or fully informed about something.

chapters.name: Unit 5 PASSAGE Ⅱ New Words

words.ex: He supports advocacy for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他支持清洁用水的倡导。
words.en: The act of pleading or arguing in favor of something, such as a cause, idea, or policy; active support.

words.tr: adj. 讨厌的； v. “annoy”的现在分词；
words.ex: The loud noise is annoying.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音很讨厌。
words.en: Something that is annoying makes you feel fairly angry and impatient.

words.tr:
n. 奖品；裁定；
v. 授予；
words.ex: He received an award for best student.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了最佳学生奖。
words.en: An award is a prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement.

words.tr:
adj. 湿漉漉的；乱蓬蓬的；全身泥污的；脏兮兮的
v. 弄脏；弄湿；弄皱；“bedraggle”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The dog came in bedraggled after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 狗在雨后湿漉漉地进来了。
words.en: If someone or something is bedraggled, they look untidy because they are wet and dirty.

words.tr: n. 露天看台；露天座位
words.ex: The fans filled the bleachers to watch the game.
words.ex_cn: 球迷们填满了露天看台观看比赛。
words.en: The bleachers are the raised, tiered rows of benches found at sports fields and other venues, where spectators sit to watch the event.

words.ex: He beat his competitor in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中击败了对手。
words.en: A competitor is a person, team, or company that is competing against others, especially in business or sports.

words.tr: v. 集中；浓缩；“concentrate”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 浓缩的；密集的；全神贯注的；
words.ex: He concentrated on his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他专心做作业。
words.en: If something is concentrated, it has been made stronger or purer by removing or reducing the amount of other substances in it.

words.tr: n. 分户出售公寓大厦（等于 condominium）; n. （Condo）人名；（意）孔多
words.ex: He bought a condo near the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一套靠近海滩的公寓。
words.en: A condo is an apartment in a building with several apartments, each of which is owned by the people living in it.

words.ex: He went to the dental clinic for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去牙科诊所做检查。
words.en: Relating to the teeth or to the work of a dentist.

words.tr:
v. （使）滴下；流口水；运球
n. 点滴；少量；口水
words.ex: The tap continues to dribble water.
words.ex_cn: 水龙头一直在滴水。
words.en: If a liquid dribbles somewhere, or if you dribble it, it drops down slowly or flows in a thin stream. In sports such as football and basketball, if you dribble the ball, you keep kicking or tapping it in order to keep it moving.

words.ex: He felt tired after the exertion of running up the hill.
words.ex_cn: 在努力跑上山后，他感到很累。
words.en: The use of physical or mental energy; hard work.

words.tr: n. 枯竭；耗尽；筋疲力尽；
words.ex: The long hike led to his exhaustion.
words.ex_cn: 长时间的徒步旅行导致他筋疲力尽。
words.en: A state of extreme physical or mental tiredness.

words.tr: adj. 毫无表情的；面无表情的
words.ex: He gave an expressionless look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时，面无表情。
words.en: If someone's face is expressionless, it shows no feeling, emotion, or thought.

words.tr: n. 女性特质；女性气质
words.ex: She shows her femininity through gentle words and kind actions.
words.ex_cn: 她通过温柔的话语和善良的举动展现女性气质。
words.en: Femininity refers to the qualities or attributes regarded as characteristic of women or girls.

words.tr: adj. 镶褶边的; 百叶裙
words.ex: The little girl wears a frilly dress.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩穿着一件花边裙子。
words.en: Something that is frilly is decorated with a lot of gathered or pleated fabric, often in a way that is considered old-fashioned or overly decorative.

words.ex: He changed his hairstyle last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周换了发型。
words.en: A hairstyle is the way in which someone's hair is cut and arranged.

words.ex: She put honey on her toast.
words.ex_cn: 她在吐司上涂了蜂蜜。
words.en: Honey is a sweet, sticky, yellowish-brown fluid made by bees and other insects from nectar collected from flowers.

words.tr:
n. 箍；环；圈
v. 加箍于；围绕
words.ex: The barrel is held together by a wooden hoop.
words.ex_cn: 这个桶由一个木制的箍固定在一起。
words.en: A hoop is a large ring made of wood, metal, or plastic, used in games or as a decoration.

words.ex: The horror of the dark made her scream.
words.ex_cn: 对黑暗的恐惧让她尖叫。
words.en: A feeling of great fear, shock, or disgust.

words.ex: His silence implies he disagrees.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默暗示他不同意。
words.en: To suggest or indicate something indirectly rather than stating it explicitly.

words.ex: The dark clouds are an indication of rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是下雨的迹象。
words.en: An indication is a sign which suggests, for example, what people are thinking or feeling.

words.ex: He showed indifference to his friend's problems.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的问题表现出冷淡。
words.en: Indifference is the state of being indifferent, especially in the sense of not caring or being uninterested.

words.tr: adj. 侮辱的； v. “insult”的现在分词；
words.ex: His insulting words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他侮辱的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's remarks or actions as insulting, you mean they are rude and offensive.

words.ex: He spoke in a lawyerlike way to sound serious.
words.ex_cn: 他以像律师一样的方式说话，以显得严肃。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a lawyer; typical of the behavior or manner of a lawyer.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.ex: She put on mascara before the party.
words.ex_cn: 她在派对前涂了睫毛膏。
words.en: Mascara is a cosmetic substance that you put on your eyelashes to make them look darker and longer.

words.ex: He always follows his morality in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他日常生活中总是遵循自己的道德。
words.en: Morality is the belief that some behaviour is right and acceptable and that other behaviour is wrong.

words.tr: adj. 泥泞的；模糊不清的；
words.ex: The road became muddy after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，这条路变得泥泞。
words.en: If something is muddy, it is covered in mud or full of mud. If you muddy something, you make it muddy or you make it less clear or more complicated.

words.ex: She wears her hair in a ponytail.
words.ex_cn: 她把头发扎成马尾辫。
words.en: A hairstyle in which the hair is pulled back and tied at the back of the head, resembling the tail of a pony.

words.tr: n. 正式舞会，毕业舞会
words.ex: He wore a suit to the prom.
words.ex_cn: 他穿西装去参加毕业舞会。
words.en: A prom is a formal dance held for a high school or college class, typically at the end of the academic year.

words.tr:
n. 请求；要求的事；
v. 要求；请求；
words.ex: He made a request for help.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个帮助的请求。
words.en: If you request something, you ask for it politely or formally.

words.ex: It was a rainy day, so we stayed inside.
words.ex_cn: 那天是多雨的，所以我们待在室内。
words.en: If the weather is rainy, it is raining a lot.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.ex: She tied a red ribbon around the box.
words.ex_cn: 她把一条红色的带状物系在盒子上。
words.en: A ribbon is a long, narrow piece of cloth that you use for tying things together or as a decoration.

words.ex: He plays soccer every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末踢足球。
words.en: Soccer is a game played between two teams of eleven players who try to score by kicking or heading a ball into the opposing team's goal.

words.ex: She plays softball every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 她每个周末都打垒球。
words.en: A game similar to baseball but played on a smaller field and with a larger, softer ball.

words.ex: He left the party, and subsequently went home.
words.ex_cn: 他离开了派对，随后回家了。
words.en: If something happens subsequently, it happens after something else.

words.ex: He wore a sweatband to keep sweat out of his eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一条护腕，以防汗水流进眼睛。
words.en: A sweatband is a band of material worn around the head or wrist to absorb sweat.

words.ex: My teammate helped me win the game.
words.ex_cn: 我的队友帮我赢得了比赛。
words.en: A teammate is a fellow member of a team.

words.ex: He will try out for the soccer team tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天将参加足球队的选拔。
words.en: A tryout is an opportunity to show that you are suitable for a particular job or activity, especially in sports or acting.

words.tr:
n. 大学；校队
adj. 大学代表队的
words.ex: He plays football for varsity.
words.ex_cn: 他为大学足球队打球。
words.en: A varsity is the principal team representing a university, college, or school in sports, games, or other competitions.

words.ex: He signed his name in the yearbook.
words.ex_cn: 他在年鉴上签了自己的名字。
words.en: A yearbook is a book published annually by a school, college, or university, recording the events and achievements of the previous year and often containing photographs of students and faculty.

chapters.name: Unit 5 PASSAGE Ⅱ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrasal verb. 与…紧密相关；与…有密切联系
words.ex: His success is bound up with hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的成功与努力工作紧密相关。
words.en: To be closely connected or involved with something.

words.tr: phrase. 面对（困难、挑战或强大对手）；与……对抗；处境艰难
words.ex: He is up against a tough opponent in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 他在决赛中面对一个强大的对手。
words.en: To be facing or confronting a difficult situation or opponent.

words.tr: phrase. 遭到批评；受到指责
words.ex: He came in for criticism after the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他犯错后受到了批评。
words.en: To be subjected to criticism or disapproval.

words.tr: phrase. 遭受责备；受到批评
words.ex: He will come in for blame if the plan fails.
words.ex_cn: 如果计划失败，他会受到责备。
words.en: To receive criticism or blame for something.

words.tr: phrase. 选择；追求；努力争取
words.ex: I want to go for the blue shirt.
words.ex_cn: 我对那件蓝色的衬衫感兴趣。
words.en: If you go for something, you choose it or try to achieve it.

words.tr: phrase. 健康；在外形上；处于良好状态
words.ex: He runs every day to stay in shape.
words.ex_cn: 他每天跑步以保持健康。
words.en: In good physical condition; healthy.

words.tr: phrase. v. （指突然意识到某事）逐渐被明白，开始理解
words.ex: It dawned on him that he forgot his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他突然意识到自己忘了钥匙。
words.en: If a fact dawns on you, you realize it gradually.

words.tr: phrase. v. （指某事）突然被某人意识到，逐渐被某人明白
words.ex: It finally dawned on him that he forgot his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他终于意识到自己忘了带钥匙。
words.en: If a fact or idea dawns on you, you realize it for the first time.

words.tr: phrase. 与……相配；与……协调；与……很搭
words.ex: This shirt goes well with those pants.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫和那条裤子很相配。
words.en: To be suitable or appropriate in combination with something else.

words.tr: phrase. 签约参加工作；签约雇用；报名
words.ex: He signed up for a job at the local factory.
words.ex_cn: 他签约参加了当地工厂的工作。
words.en: To agree to become involved in an organized activity or to join a group or organization.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人以…印象；使某人觉得…
words.ex: The quiet town strike someone as peaceful.
words.ex_cn: 这个安静的小镇给人留下平和的印象。
words.en: If something strikes you as a particular thing, it seems to be that thing.

chapters.name: Unit 6 Part Two New Words

words.ex: He was late, so he left accordingly.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，于是相应地提前出发了。
words.en: In a way that is appropriate to the particular circumstances.

words.ex: The soldier wore an armored vest.
words.ex_cn: 这名士兵穿着一件装甲背心。
words.en: Covered with or protected by armor.

words.tr: adj. 装甲的，武装的; 配备有装甲车辆的; 蛇皮管的
words.ex: The soldier wore an armoured vest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿了一件装甲背心。
words.en: Protected by or equipped with armour.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.tr: adj. 决定性的；权威性的；确定的；
words.ex: The test results were definitive.
words.ex_cn: 这些检测结果是决定性的。
words.en: A definitive book, performance, or report is considered to be the best of its kind that has ever been done or that will ever be done.

words.ex: The denominator is 5 in the fraction 3/5.
words.ex_cn: 在分数 3/5 中，分母是 5。
words.en: The number below the line in a fraction that shows the number of equal parts into which the whole is divided.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a big disaster.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了一场大灾难。
words.en: A disaster is an unexpected event causing great damage, destruction, or distress.

words.ex: The worker had long exposure to loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人长期暴露在噪音中。
words.en: The condition of being exposed to something, especially to something harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: A fraction of the students passed the test.
words.ex_cn: 只有一小部分学生通过了考试。
words.en: A fraction is a small part or amount of something.

words.tr: n. 疑病症; 忧郁症，疑病症，季肋部( hypochondrium的名词复数 )
words.ex: Her hypochondria led her to visit the doctor frequently.
words.ex_cn: 她的疑病症使她频繁地去看医生。
words.en: Hypochondria is a condition in which a person is excessively and unduly worried about having a serious illness.

words.tr:
n. 疑病症患者
adj. 患疑病症的
words.ex: He is a hypochondriac who thinks he is sick every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是个疑病症患者，每天都觉得自己生病了。
words.en: A hypochondriac is a person who is excessively anxious about their health and often believes they are suffering from a serious illness despite having no or only mild symptoms.

words.ex: The road closure caused an inconvenience to commuters.
words.ex_cn: 道路封闭给通勤者带来了不便。
words.en: Inconvenience refers to the state or quality of being inconvenient; trouble or difficulty caused to one's personal requirements or comfort.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: Please inform me when the meeting starts.
words.ex_cn: 请在会议开始时通知我。
words.en: To inform someone means to tell them about something.

words.ex: He got an injury while playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他在踢足球时受了伤。
words.en: An injury is damage to your body. It is a general term that refers to harm caused by accidents, falls, hits, weapons, etc.

words.ex: The miner works deep underground.
words.ex_cn: 矿工在地下深处工作。
words.en: A miner is a person who works in a mine, extracting coal, gold, or other minerals.

words.ex: The bacteria multiply quickly.
words.ex_cn: 细菌迅速增加。
words.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example, 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

words.tr:
adj. 神经（官能）症的；神经质的；神经过敏的
n. 神经官能症患者；神经质者；神经过敏者
words.ex: She had a neurotic fear of flying.
words.ex_cn: 她对飞行有一种神经质的恐惧。
words.en: If you say that someone is neurotic, you mean that they are always worried or anxious about things that you consider unimportant.

words.ex: The numerator is 5 in the fraction 5/8.
words.ex_cn: 在分数 5/8 中，分子是 5。
words.en: The numerator is the top number in a fraction that shows how many parts of the whole are being considered.

words.ex: He only read the partial report.
words.ex_cn: 他只读了部分报告。
words.en: If you describe something as partial, you mean that it is not complete or whole.

words.ex: The physician checked the patient's temperature.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了病人的体温。
words.en: A physician is a medical doctor who is trained in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases and injuries.

words.ex: The probability of rain tomorrow is high.
words.ex_cn: 明天下雨的概率很高。
words.en: A probability is a measure of how likely it is that some event will occur.

words.ex: The ratio of boys to girls is 3 to 2.
words.ex_cn: 男孩与女孩的比例是3比2。
words.en: A ratio is a relationship between two numbers indicating how many times the first number contains the second.

words.ex: It's risky to walk alone at night.
words.ex_cn: 晚上独自走路是危险的。
words.en: If an activity or action is risky, it is dangerous or likely to fail.

words.tr: n. 富有冒险性的事，危险重重
words.ex: The riskiness of the investment made many investors hesitant.
words.ex_cn: 这项投资的冒险性使得许多投资者犹豫不决。
words.en: The quality or state of being risky; the degree to which something is risky.

words.ex: The thieves robbed the bank last night.
words.ex_cn: 小偷昨晚抢劫了银行。
words.en: To rob someone or somewhere means to take money or property illegally from them, often using force.

words.ex: There are roughly 100 students in the class.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级大约有100名学生。
words.en: In a manner that is not exact or detailed; approximately.

words.ex: He has a high fever as a symptom of the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧是流感的症状。
words.en: A symptom is a physical or mental feature which is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly such a feature that is apparent to the patient.

words.ex: The red team played versus the blue team.
words.ex_cn: 红队与蓝队比赛。
words.en: Used to indicate the two sides in a competition or conflict.

chapters.name: Unit 6 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 各种各样的；各种类型的
words.ex: He has all manner of books in his room.
words.ex_cn: 他的房间里有各种各样的书。
words.en: used to indicate a wide variety of something

words.tr: phrase. 结束；告终；意外到达
words.ex: He didn't plan to stay, but he ended up sleeping there.
words.ex_cn: 他本没打算留下，但最后在那里睡了。
words.en: If you end up in a particular place or situation, you are in that place or situation after a series of events, even though you did not originally intend to be.

words.ex: Wolves feed on deer in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 狼在森林里以鹿为食。
words.en: To consume something as food or to derive nourishment from it.

words.tr: phrase. 正在考虑；正被谈论的；讨论中的；可怀疑
words.ex: The job in question is still available.
words.ex_cn: 正在讨论的工作仍然空缺。
words.en: The person, thing, or group that is in question is the one that you have been talking about or that is involved in the situation you are discussing.

words.tr: phrase. 很可能；完全有可能；大可
words.ex: He may well win the race, he trains every day.
words.ex_cn: 他很可能赢得比赛，他每天都训练。
words.en: used to say that something is likely to happen or be true

words.ex: He got the job on the strength of his impressive portfolio.
words.ex_cn: 他凭借令人印象深刻的简历得到了这份工作。
words.en: If you do something on the strength of something, you do it because you believe that it is good enough or strong enough to support your action.

words.tr: phrase. 把……减少到；把……简化为；使……沦为；使……变成
words.ex: They reduce the price to $5.
words.ex_cn: 他们把价格降到了5美元。
words.en: To bring something to a smaller or less complicated state.

chapters.name: Unit 6 PASSAGE Ⅰ New Words

words.tr: abbr. 艾滋病；获得性免疫缺乏综合症；“Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome”的缩写；
words.ex: He got tested for aids last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周做了艾滋病检测。
words.en: AIDS is a disease caused by a virus that weakens a person's immune system, making them vulnerable to other infections and diseases.

words.ex: The earthquake caused catastrophic damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: A catastrophic event or situation is one that causes great damage or suffering.

words.ex: The new phone is too costly for me.
words.ex_cn: 这部新手机对我来说太贵了。
words.en: If you say that something is costly, you mean that it costs a lot of money, often more than you would want to pay.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.ex: The rich pay disproportionately more taxes.
words.ex_cn: 富人缴纳的税不成比例地更多。
words.en: To an extent that is too large or too small in comparison with something else.

words.ex: The movie was enormously popular.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极度受欢迎。
words.en: To a very great degree or extent; extremely.

words.tr: n. 资金；款项；拨款； v. “fund”的现在分词；
words.ex: The school needs more funding for new books.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校需要更多资金来购买新书。
words.en: Funding is money which is used to pay for a particular activity or to help achieve a particular purpose.

words.ex: It rained all day, hence the game was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 下了一整天的雨，因此比赛被取消了。
words.en: You use hence to indicate that the statement you are about to make is a consequence of what you have just said.

words.tr: n. 即时性；直接性；迫切性
words.ex: The immediacy of the response surprised her.
words.ex_cn: 回复的即时性让她感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being immediate or happening without delay.

words.ex: The incidence of flu increased last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感的发生率上升了。
words.en: The incidence of something is the frequency with which it occurs or the rate at which it happens.

words.ex: The incubation of eggs takes about 21 days.
words.ex_cn: 鸡蛋的孵化需要大约21天。
words.en: The process of keeping eggs at the right temperature so that they develop and hatch, or the period of time that a disease takes to develop before symptoms appear.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的；不重要的；
words.ex: The mistake was insignificant and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误无关紧要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as insignificant, you mean that they are small or unimportant, and therefore not worth considering seriously.

words.ex: The police caught the killer last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚抓到了杀手。
words.en: A killer is a person, animal, or thing that kills.

words.tr:
n. 滞后；延迟；
v. 落后；缓慢移动；
words.ex: There is a lag between the signal and the response.
words.ex_cn: 信号和响应之间有滞后。
words.en: If one thing or person lags behind another thing or person, their progress is slower than that of the other.

words.ex: He chose the lesser price.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了更少的价格。
words.en: You use lesser to indicate that something is smaller in extent, degree, or amount than another thing that has been mentioned.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.ex: It was raining, nonetheless, we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天下着雨，尽管如此，我们还是去散步了。
words.en: Nonetheless is used to indicate that something is true or happens in spite of what has just been said.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；著名的；
words.ex: This is a notable achievement.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个值得注意的成就。
words.en: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable.

words.ex: The bill is payable next week.
words.ex_cn: 这笔账单下周应付。
words.en: If an amount of money is payable, it has to be paid or it can be paid.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.tr: n. 管乐器吹奏者，风笛吹奏者；管道工；绿鳍鱼；<罕>气喘的马; 【名】 （Piper）（法、塞、瑞...
words.ex: The piper played a haunting melody on his bagpipes.
words.ex_cn: 风笛手用他的风笛演奏了一首令人难忘的旋律。
words.en: A piper is someone who plays a pipe, especially a bagpipe.

words.ex: The poll showed that most people support the new law.
words.ex_cn: 这项民意调查表明，大多数人支持这项新法律。
words.en: A poll is a survey in which people are asked their opinions about something, usually in order to find out how popular something is or what people intend to do in the future.

words.ex: His preoccupation with video games made him ignore his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的全神贯注让他忽略了作业。
words.en: If you have a preoccupation with something or someone, you think or worry about them very often and they are the main focus of your attention.

words.ex: He is principally responsible for the project.
words.ex_cn: 他主要负责这个项目。
words.en: Mainly; for the most part.

words.ex: The sun gives off radiation.
words.ex_cn: 太阳发出辐射。
words.en: Radiation is energy that comes from a source and travels through space at the speed of light. This energy has an electric field and a magnetic field associated with it, and has wave-like properties. You could also call radiation 'electromagnetic waves'.

words.ex: He asked for a reassessment of his test score.
words.ex_cn: 他要求重新评估他的考试成绩。
words.en: A reassessment is a new appraisal or evaluation.

words.ex: He repeatedly asked for help.
words.ex_cn: 他再三地请求帮助。
words.en: If something is done repeatedly, it is done again and again.

words.ex: The seriousness of the accident surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故的严重性让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality or state of being serious.

words.tr: adj. 近视的；目光短浅的
words.ex: He is short-sighted and needs glasses to see far.
words.ex_cn: 他近视，需要戴眼镜才能看远。
words.en: If someone is short-sighted, they cannot see things clearly that are far away, or they do not plan for the future in a sensible way.

words.ex: He explained the rules specifically.
words.ex_cn: 他具体地解释了规则。
words.en: You use specifically to emphasize that something is given special attention and considered separately from other things of the same kind.

words.ex: The movie caused a feeling of terror in the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让观众感到恐怖。
words.en: Terror is a very strong feeling of fear, especially fear that you experience suddenly.

words.ex: His explanation was understandable.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释是可以理解的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or feelings as understandable, you mean that they have reacted to a situation in a natural way or in the way you would expect.

chapters.name: Unit 6 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 使某人感到极度恐惧；令某人心惊胆战
words.ex: The loud noise strike terror into the child's heart.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的响声让那个孩子心中充满了恐惧。
words.en: To cause someone to feel extreme fear.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人感到恐惧；令某人心生畏惧
words.ex: The loud thunder strike fear into the little boy's heart.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的雷声让那个小男孩心生恐惧。
words.en: To cause someone to feel very afraid.

words.tr: 短语动词. 使某事物得到控制；将某事物控制住
words.ex: The firefighters brought the fire under control quickly.
words.ex_cn: 消防员很快把火势控制住了。
words.en: To gain control over something, especially a difficult situation or problem.

words.ex: Bear in mind that the bus leaves at 6 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 请记住，公交车晚上6点发车。
words.en: If you tell someone to bear something in mind, you are reminding or warning them about something important which they should remember.

words.tr: phrase. 讲得通； 有意义； 言之有理
words.ex: This plan makes sense.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有道理。
words.en: To be reasonable or understandable.

words.tr: phrase. 在这种光线（或光亮）下；从这个角度来看；鉴于此
words.ex: In this light, the painting looks different.
words.ex_cn: 在这种光线（或光亮）下，这幅画看起来不一样了。
words.en: From this perspective or point of view.

words.ex: He passed the test by virtue of his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他凭借努力学习通过了考试。
words.en: Because of or as a result of something.

chapters.name: Unit 6 PASSAGE Ⅱ New Words

words.tr: adj. 有冒险精神的；敢于创新的；
words.ex: He is an adventurous boy who loves climbing mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢爬山的有冒险精神的男孩。
words.en: Willing to take risks or to try out new methods, ideas, or experiences.

words.ex: The alpine flowers bloom in the high mountains.
words.ex_cn: 高山上的花朵在高山上绽放。
words.en: Relating to high mountains, especially the Alps.

words.ex: His ambition is to become a president.
words.ex_cn: 他的野心是成为总统。
words.en: An ambition is a strong desire to achieve something, typically requiring determination and hard work.

words.ex: He twisted his ankle while running.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑步时扭伤了脚踝。
words.en: The joint between the foot and the leg, in which movement occurs in two planes.

words.ex: He jumped off the bridge with a bungee.
words.ex_cn: 他带着一根蹦极索从桥上跳了下去。
words.en: A bungee is a long elastic cord used in bungee jumping or for securing objects.

words.ex: The bees made a loud buzz near the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂在花附近发出嗡嗡声。
words.en: To make a low, continuous, humming or sibilant sound, like that made by bees or flies.

words.ex: He capitalized on the chance to start a business.
words.ex_cn: 他利用了这个创业的机会。
words.en: To capitalize means to use something to your advantage, especially in a way that brings financial gain. It can also mean to write or print a word with its first letter as a capital letter.

words.ex: The guitarist played a C major chord.
words.ex_cn: 吉他手弹了一个C大和弦。
words.en: A chord is a group of three or more musical notes played together.

words.ex: The lawyer helped her client with the contract.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助她的客户处理合同。
words.en: A client is a person or organization receiving services or advice from a professional or company.

words.ex: He tied the box with a red cord.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根红绳把盒子绑了起来。
words.en: A cord is a thick string or thin rope made of twisted strands, or something resembling such a string or rope in appearance or function.

words.ex: The rubber band is elastic.
words.ex_cn: 橡皮筋是有弹性的。
words.en: An elastic material is able to stretch and then return to its original shape or size.

words.tr: n. 阐述者；拥护者；代表者；指数
words.ex: He is the exponent of modern education reform.
words.ex_cn: 他是现代教育改革的阐述者。
words.en: An exponent is someone who supports and explains a particular idea, theory, or system, or a symbol that shows how many times a number is to be multiplied by itself.

words.ex: The car accident caused one fatality.
words.ex_cn: 这场车祸导致一人死亡。
words.en: A fatality is a death caused by an accident or by violence, or is the fact of causing death.

words.ex: The glacier moves slowly down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 冰川缓慢地沿着山向下移动。
words.en: A glacier is a large, persistent body of ice that forms where the accumulation of snow exceeds its ablation over many years, often centuries.

words.ex: The hikers walked through a deep gorge.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者走过一个深峡谷。
words.en: A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, often carved by a river. It can also refer to the act of eating greedily.

words.ex: He filed a lawsuit against the company.
words.ex_cn: 他向这家公司提起了诉讼。
words.en: A lawsuit is a case in a court of law which concerns a dispute between two people or organizations.

words.tr:
n. 最大限度；最大量；
adj. 最大极限的；最多的；
words.ex: The maximum of the crowd is 100 people.
words.ex_cn: 人群的上限是100人。
words.en: The greatest or highest amount possible or attained.

words.tr: n. 登山者，登山运动员
words.ex: The mountaineer successfully reached the summit after a long and arduous climb.
words.ex_cn: 经过漫长而艰难的攀登，这名登山者成功到达了山顶。
words.en: A mountaineer is someone who climbs mountains as a sport or profession.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr:
n. 降落伞
v. 跳伞；用降落伞空投
words.ex: He jumped from the plane and opened his parachute.
words.ex_cn: 他从飞机上跳下并打开了降落伞。
words.en: A parachute is a device used to slow the motion of an object through an atmosphere by creating drag.

words.ex: He was a pioneer in space exploration.
words.ex_cn: 他是太空探索的先驱者。
words.en: A pioneer is someone who is one of the first people to do something that others will later develop or continue. Pioneers are also people who are among the first to go to live in a new area, especially in the past when people were trying to settle in new lands.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的； v. 取得资格；“qualify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a qualified teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有资格的老师。
words.en: Having the necessary qualifications for a particular job or task.

words.tr:
v. 引用；报价；
n. 引用；引文；报价；
words.ex: He quoted Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中引用了莎士比亚的话。
words.en: To repeat or copy out (a group of words from a text or speech), typically with an indication that one is not the original author or speaker.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.tr: v. 使清洁；进行消毒；净化
words.ex: The water is sanitized to remove harmful bacteria.
words.ex_cn: 水经过消毒以去除有害细菌。
words.en: To sanitize something means to make it clean and free from bacteria, in order to prevent disease.

words.tr: n. 寻求者；追求者；搜索者
words.ex: The seeker found a hidden path in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这位寻找者在森林里发现了一条隐蔽的小路。
words.en: Someone who is trying to find or obtain something.

words.ex: He likes to ski in the mountains during winter.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在冬天去山里滑雪。
words.en: A ski is one of a pair of long, flat runners attached to the feet for gliding over snow. Skiing is the activity of gliding over snow on skis.

words.ex: The statistics show a rise in sales last year.
words.ex_cn: 这些统计数字显示去年销售额有所上升。
words.en: Statistics is a branch of mathematics dealing with the collection, analysis, interpretation, presentation, and organization of data.

words.ex: He moved to suburbia to raise his family.
words.ex_cn: 他搬到郊区去抚养他的家庭。
words.en: Suburbia refers to the residential areas on the outskirts of a city or large town, often characterized by single-family homes, quiet streets, and a sense of community.

words.ex: He will sue the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 他将起诉这家公司要求赔偿。
words.en: To sue means to start a legal case against someone, usually to claim money from them because they have caused you harm or loss.

words.tr:
n. 激浪；拍岸浪花；
v. 冲浪；（互联网上）冲浪；
words.ex: He bought a new surf for the beach trip.
words.ex_cn: 他为海滩之旅买了一块新的激浪。
words.en: To surf means to ride on the crest of a wave towards the shore, typically on a surfboard. It can also mean to browse the internet.

words.tr:
n. 摇摆；
v. 摇摆；
words.ex: The child enjoyed the swing at the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子喜欢在公园里荡秋千。
words.en: If something swings or if you swing it, it moves repeatedly backwards and forwards or from side to side from a fixed point. If you swing somewhere, you move there by holding onto something and moving your body through the air.

words.tr: n. 损失；伤亡人数；通行费；
words.ex: The war caused a heavy toll on innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 战争给平民带来了巨大的损失。
words.en: A toll is a small sum of money that you have to pay in order to use a particular bridge or road. / A toll is the total number of deaths, accidents, or disasters that occur in a particular period of time. / When a bell tolls, it rings slowly and repeatedly, often as a sign that someone has died.

words.ex: She typically arrives early for class.
words.ex_cn: 她往往很早就到课。
words.en: You use typically to say that something usually happens in the way that you are describing.

words.ex: The urban area has many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市地区有许多高楼。
words.en: relating to a city or town

words.ex: He hurt his wrist while playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他打篮球时伤了手腕。
words.en: The part of your body where your hand joins your arm.

chapters.name: Unit 6 PASSAGE Ⅱ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrasal verb. 利用（机会、优势等）；从……中获利
words.ex: They decided to capitalize on the success of their previous album.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定利用上一张专辑的成功。
words.en: To capitalize on something means to use a situation or opportunity to gain an advantage for yourself.

words.tr: phrase. （在…到…之间）变化；范围从…到…
words.ex: The prices range from 5 dollars to 10 dollars.
words.ex_cn: 价格从5美元到10美元不等。
words.en: If things range from one thing to another, they vary within these limits on a scale of measurement or quality.

words.ex: The children line up to enter the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们排队进入教室。
words.en: To arrange people or things in a row or to arrange for an event or activity to happen.

words.ex: He found a shortcut to school.
words.ex_cn: 他找到了一条去学校的捷径。
words.en: A quicker or more direct way to get somewhere or do something.

words.tr: phrase. 引起共鸣；触动情感（尤指唤起熟悉或强烈的情感反应）
words.ex: The song strikes a chord with many people.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌引起了许多人的共鸣。
words.en: To cause someone to feel sympathy, emotion, or enthusiasm.

chapters.name: Unit 7 Part Two New Words

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.tr: n. 开始；毕业典礼；学位授予典礼
words.ex: The commencement of the class was at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程的开始时间是上午9点。
words.en: The commencement of something is its beginning.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.ex: He finished his homework before the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 他在截止日期前完成了作业。
words.en: A deadline is a time or date before which a particular task must be finished or a particular thing must be done.

words.ex: He erased the wrong answer with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他用橡皮擦掉了错误的答案。
words.en: To erase something means to remove it completely from a surface or from a place where it is stored.

words.ex: The faculty of engineering has many labs.
words.ex_cn: 工程学院有许多实验室。
words.en: A faculty is a group of departments in a university or college that specialize in a particular subject or group of subjects, or the teachers in such a group.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.tr:
adj. 最终的；最后的；
n. 决赛；
words.ex: This is the final answer.
words.ex_cn: 这是最终的答案。
words.en: Last in a series or coming at the end of a process.

words.tr:
adj. 宽恕的；宽大的；仁慈的
v. 原谅；宽恕；“forgive”的现在分词
words.ex: She is a forgiving person who forgets mistakes easily.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个宽恕的人，容易忘记错误。
words.en: If you describe someone as forgiving, you mean that they are kind and tolerant towards someone who has hurt them or done something wrong.

words.ex: The teacher will formulate a new rule for class.
words.ex_cn: 老师将制定一条新的课堂规则。
words.en: If you formulate something such as a plan or proposal, you invent it, thinking about the details carefully.

words.tr: adj. 絮聒的；饶舌的；多嘴的
words.ex: He is garrulous and talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他话很多，说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as garrulous, you mean that they talk a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.tr: adj. 了解情况的； v. 通知；告知；“inform”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is an informed voter who reads the news daily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个了解情况的选民，每天阅读新闻。
words.en: If someone is informed, they know a lot about a particular subject or situation.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr:
adj. 期中的
n. 期中考试
words.ex: He is preparing for his midterm exam next week.
words.ex_cn: 他正在为下周的期中考试做准备。
words.en: A midterm is an examination that is given in the middle of a term in a school or college.

words.tr: adj. 无痛苦的；不痛的；无需努力（工作）的
words.ex: The injection was painless.
words.ex_cn: 这次注射没有疼痛。
words.en: If you describe something as painless, you mean that it is easy to do or causes you no trouble or suffering.

words.tr:
adj. 危险的；难对付的
adv. 非常地；极度地
words.ex: The situation was parlous, and we had to tread carefully.
words.ex_cn: 情况非常危险，我们必须小心行事。
words.en: A parlous situation is full of danger or uncertainty.

words.ex: He took a preparatory course before starting university.
words.ex_cn: 他在上大学之前参加了一个预备课程。
words.en: Preparatory means relating to or done in preparation for something.

words.ex: He gave a presentation about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个关于气候变化的报告。
words.en: The act of showing or explaining something to an audience.

words.tr: n. 伪装；假象；虚伪的表现
words.ex: He was accused of using pretense to gain sympathy.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控利用伪装来博取同情。
words.en: A pretense is an action or way of behaving that is intended to make people believe something that is not true.

words.tr: n. 轻易放弃的人；半途而废者
words.ex: He was labeled a quitter after he dropped out of the marathon.
words.ex_cn: 他在马拉松比赛中途退出后，被贴上了半途而废者的标签。
words.en: A quitter is someone who gives up easily and does not finish something they have started.

words.tr: adj. 马虎的；敷衍了事的
words.ex: He gave a slipshod answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个敷衍的回答。
words.en: If something is slipshod, it is done in a careless or lazy way, without attention to detail.

words.ex: He is supposedly coming tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 据推测他明天来。
words.en: If you say that something is supposedly the case, you mean that people say it is the case but you do not think it is necessarily true.

words.ex: My teacher is tolerant of different opinions.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师对不同的观点很宽容。
words.en: If you describe someone as tolerant, you approve of the fact that they allow other people to say and do as they like, even if they do not agree with or like it.

words.tr:
v. 成为三倍；使增至三倍；
n. 三倍的数；三个一组；
adj. 三部分的；
words.ex: The company's profits tripled last year.
words.ex_cn: 该公司去年的利润增长了三倍。
words.en: To triple something means to make it three times as much in size or number.

words.ex: The task was unchallenging and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这项任务没有挑战性，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as unchallenging, you mean that it is not difficult or demanding, and therefore not likely to be interesting or exciting.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏想象力的；无趣的
words.ex: He gave an unimaginative answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个缺乏创意的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimaginative, you are criticizing them because they do not think of new or interesting ideas or things.

words.ex: He tries to unlearn bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 他试图改掉坏习惯。
words.en: If you unlearn something that you have learned, you try to forget it or ignore it, often because it is wrong or it is causing you problems.

chapters.name: Unit 7 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 将...付诸行动；把…表演出来
words.ex: He didn't just talk about the plan—he decided to act it out.
words.ex_cn: 他不仅仅谈论这个计划，他还决定将它付诸行动。
words.en: To perform something, such as a play or a story, especially by acting; to express thoughts or feelings through actions.

words.ex: I want to be rid of this old furniture.
words.ex_cn: 我想摆脱这些旧家具。
words.en: To be free of something or someone that is unwanted or troublesome.

words.ex: He is by no means lazy.
words.ex_cn: 他绝对不懒。
words.en: You use 'by no means' to emphasize that something is not true or is definitely not the case.

words.tr: phrase. 着手做；开始认真做
words.ex: He got down to work after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后开始认真工作。
words.en: To begin to do or deal with something seriously or with determination.

words.tr: phrase. 回顾；回想；追忆（过去的事情）
words.ex: I look back on my childhood with happiness.
words.ex_cn: 我满怀幸福地回忆我的童年。
words.en: To think about something that happened in the past.

words.tr: phrase. 仔细查看；认真审视
words.ex: You should take a close look at the contract before signing it.
words.ex_cn: 你应该在签字前仔细看一下合同。
words.en: To examine something carefully and in detail.

words.tr: phrase. 仔细查看；认真审视
words.ex: You should take a close look at the contract before signing it.
words.ex_cn: 在签署合同之前，你应该仔细看一下。
words.en: To examine something carefully or in detail.

chapters.name: Unit 7 PASSAGE Ⅰ New Words

words.ex: The administrator fixed the computer system.
words.ex_cn: 管理人员修复了计算机系统。
words.en: An administrator is a person whose job involves helping to organize and supervise the way that an organization or institution functions.

words.ex: The ancient text contained arcane symbols that no one could understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本古籍中包含着无人能理解的晦涩难解的符号。
words.en: Arcane refers to something that is mysterious or difficult to understand, often because it is known or understood by only a few people.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.tr: adj. 令人毛骨悚然的，令人害怕的；<美>令人沮丧的，泄气的；使人感到寒冷的; v. （使）冷却，...
words.ex: The chilling sound of the wind made everyone shiver.
words.ex_cn: 令人毛骨悚然的风声让所有人都颤抖了。
words.en: If you describe something as chilling, you mean it is frightening.

words.tr:
adj. 满足的
v. 使满足；“content”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt contented after a simple meal with his family.
words.ex_cn: 他和家人吃了一顿简单的饭后感到满足。
words.en: If you are contented, you are satisfied with your life or the situation you are in.

words.ex: The old man muttered a curse under his breath.
words.ex_cn: 老人低声嘟囔了一句诅咒。
words.en: A curse is a word or sentence that is used to wish evil or harm on someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 发狂的；精神错乱状态的
words.ex: The demented man laughed loudly in the street.
words.ex_cn: 那个精神失常的男人在街上大声笑。
words.en: Someone who is demented behaves in a wild and uncontrolled way because they are mentally ill.

words.ex: He called for help in desperation.
words.ex_cn: 他绝望地呼救。
words.en: Desperation is the feeling that you have when you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to take any risk to change it.

words.ex: The bike ride is easy because it is downhill.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车很容易，因为是下山的。
words.en: If something or someone is moving downhill or is downhill, they are moving down a slope or are towards the bottom of a hill.

words.tr: adj. 令人兴奋的； v. “exhilarate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The roller coaster ride was exhilarating.
words.ex_cn: 过山车之旅令人兴奋。
words.en: If you describe something as exhilarating, you mean that it makes you feel very happy and excited.

words.tr: adj. 寒冷的；冷淡的；性冷淡的（女子）
words.ex: The water is frigid in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的水很冰冷。
words.en: Frigid means extremely cold in temperature or lacking warmth or enthusiasm.

words.tr:
v. 上釉；上玻璃；浇浆汁于；变呆滞
n. 釉料；光滑面；覆罩的一层
words.ex: The potter glazes the clay bowl before firing it.
words.ex_cn: 陶匠在烧制前给陶碗上釉。
words.en: To glaze means to fit panes of glass into a window frame or similar structure. It can also refer to the process of applying a glossy, often transparent, coating to pottery or other materials.

words.ex: The bird glide smoothly over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在湖面上滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and continuously along, as if without effort or resistance.

words.ex: He kneel to pray every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跪下祈祷。
words.en: To kneel means to go down into a position where one or both knees are on the ground.

words.tr:
adj. 悠闲的；从容的；
adv. 悠闲地；从容地；
words.ex: He took a leisurely walk in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园里悠闲地散步。
words.en: If you do something in a leisurely way, you do it in a relaxed and unhurried manner.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；呼啸；抱怨
n. 呻吟声；萧萧声；抱怨
words.ex: He moans when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候会呻吟。
words.en: If you moan, you make a low sound, usually because you are unhappy or in pain.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
n. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
words.ex: He mutters under his breath when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 当他生气时，他会低声嘟囔。
words.en: To speak or say something in a low voice that is hard to hear, often because you are annoyed or complaining.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.ex: He had a realization that he needed to change his life.
words.ex_cn: 他领悟到自己需要改变生活。
words.en: The act of becoming fully aware of something as a fact; the achievement of something desired or anticipated.

words.tr: v. 反胃；回吐；依样复述
words.ex: He felt sick and began to regurgitate after eating the spoiled food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了变质的食物后感到恶心，开始反胃。
words.en: To bring up and expel (food) from the stomach to the mouth, as in some birds feeding their young; to repeat (information) without understanding or thought.

words.ex: The apple is rotten and smells bad.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果腐烂了，闻起来很难闻。
words.en: Something that is rotten has decayed and cannot be used for its normal purpose.

words.tr: v. 发出喀嚓声；发出嘎吱声；使变形；碾碎
words.ex: He scrunches the plastic bag in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他用手捏塑料袋发出喀嚓声。
words.en: To scrunch something means to squeeze or crush it into a smaller or tighter shape.

words.ex: He walks on the sidewalk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在人行道上走路。
words.en: A sidewalk is a path with a hard surface by the side of a road that people walk on.

words.ex: He staggered home after drinking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了后摇摇晃晃地走回家。
words.en: If you stagger, you walk very unsteadily, as if you are about to fall.

words.tr:
n. 哭泣；落泪
v. 流泪；流出
words.ex: Her weep lasted for hours after the news.
words.ex_cn: 听到消息后，她的哭泣持续了数小时。
words.en: To shed tears, especially as an expression of distress or pain.

chapters.name: Unit 7 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 尽管困难重重；在极不可能的情况下成功
words.ex: He won the race against all odds.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了所有困难赢得了比赛。
words.en: If something happens against all odds, it happens or succeeds although it seemed impossible or very unlikely.

words.tr: phrase. 咳出；勉强说出；被迫付出
words.ex: He coughed up a small piece of food.
words.ex_cn: 他咳出了一小块食物。
words.en: To expel something from the throat or lungs by coughing; to reluctantly give or pay money.

words.ex: He can play the song from memory.
words.ex_cn: 他能凭记忆演奏这首歌曲。
words.en: To perform an action or recall information without the aid of written or printed material, relying solely on one's memory.

words.tr: phrasal verb. （使）表面光滑；（使）结成釉状；（指人）目光呆滞，神情恍惚
words.ex: His eyes glaze over when he listens to long lectures.
words.ex_cn: 他听长篇讲座时眼神呆滞。
words.en: If someone's eyes glaze over, they become dull and lose expression, usually because they are bored or tired.

words.tr: phrase. 在开会；在开庭；在上课；在会期中
words.ex: The court is in session now.
words.ex_cn: 法院现在正在开庭。
words.en: If a group of people or an organization is in session, they are having a meeting or series of meetings.

words.tr: phrase. 把…锁起来；关进监狱；使（资金）冻结；关店
words.ex: He will lock up the shop at night.
words.ex_cn: 他晚上会把商店锁上。
words.en: To secure something by locking it, or to confine someone in a place by locking it.

words.tr: phrase. 闲坐着；无所事事地坐着
words.ex: They sit around and talk every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天晚上都坐着聊天。
words.en: If you sit around or sit about, you spend time doing nothing useful or interesting.

words.ex: He said he would come, and sure enough, he arrived at 7 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 他说他会来，果然，他在晚上7点到了。
words.en: As expected or predicted; indeed.

chapters.name: Unit 7 PASSAGE Ⅱ New Words

words.ex: He worked hard to attain his goals.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以达到他的目标。
words.en: If you attain something, you gain it or achieve it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: The accident was avoidable if he had slowed down.
words.ex_cn: 如果他减速了，这场事故本可以避免。
words.en: If something is avoidable, it can be prevented or not done.

words.ex: Eating vegetables is beneficial to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你的健康有益。
words.en: Promoting or enhancing well-being; advantageous.

words.tr:
v. 吹嘘；自吹自擂
adj. 一流的；极好的
words.ex: He brags about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他炫耀自己的新车。
words.en: If you brag, you say in a very proud way that you have something or have done something.

words.tr: adj. 有微风的；轻松愉快的
words.ex: The park was breezy and full of people enjoying the weather.
words.ex_cn: 公园里微风习习，到处都是享受天气的人们。
words.en: If you describe something as breezy, you mean that it is light, informal, and cheerful.

words.tr: n. 微积分学；（人体内的）结石
words.ex: He is learning calculus at school.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学校学习微积分。
words.en: Calculus is a branch of mathematics that deals with the finding and properties of derivatives and integrals of functions, by methods originally based on the summation of infinitesimal differences.

words.ex: The water in the pond is cloudy.
words.ex_cn: 池塘里的水很浑浊。
words.en: If it is cloudy, there are a lot of clouds in the sky.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.ex: He gave a definite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了肯定的答案。
words.en: If something is definite, it is firm and clear, and unlikely to be changed.

words.ex: The sky was dismal and gray all day.
words.ex_cn: 天空一整天都是阴沉灰暗的。
words.en: If you describe something as dismal, you mean that it is very bad or depressing.

words.ex: His disposition is calm and kind.
words.ex_cn: 他的性情平静而善良。
words.en: Someone's disposition is the way that they tend to behave or feel.

words.ex: The king's greed led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 国王的贪婪导致了他的没落。
words.en: The collapse of a person or organization's power, status, or success.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.ex: The unfair rule enrage him.
words.ex_cn: 不公平的规则激怒了他。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.ex: He stopped halfway to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他在半路停下来休息。
words.en: At or to a point midway between two others.

words.tr:
n. 猎犬
v. 追逐；纠缠
words.ex: The hound chased the rabbit through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎犬在森林里追赶兔子。
words.en: A hound is a type of dog used for hunting or chasing. It can also refer to someone who persistently pursues or bothers someone else.

words.tr: n. 免于惩罚；不受惩处
words.ex: He stole the money and got away with it in impunity.
words.ex_cn: 他偷了钱，却逍遥法外。
words.en: If someone does something with impunity, they do it without fear of being punished for it.

words.ex: Birds inhabit the forest near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类居住在湖边的森林里。
words.en: If a place or region is inhabited by a group of people or a species of animal, those people or animals live there.

words.tr: adj. 多虱的；可鄙的；差劲的
words.ex: The dog had a lousy coat full of fleas.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗的毛发多虱子。
words.en: If you describe something as lousy, you mean that it is of very bad quality or that you do not like it.

words.tr: adj. 残忍的；无情的；无慈悲心的；
words.ex: The merciless storm destroyed the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场残忍的风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: If you describe someone as merciless, you mean that they are very cruel or determined and do not show any concern for the effect their actions have on other people.

words.tr: adj. 有动机的；有积极性的； v. 激发；“motivate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is motivated to study hard for the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他有动力努力为考试学习。
words.en: If you are motivated by something, especially a strong emotion, it causes you to behave in a particular way.

words.tr:
v. 唠叨；喋喋不休；不断困扰
n. 老马；驽马；矮小马
words.ex: She nagged him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 她不停地催他打扫房间。
words.en: If someone nags you, they keep asking you to do something you have not done yet or do not want to do.

words.tr: n. 准确；精确；细节；细微的差别
words.ex: The nicety of the measurement surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个测量的准确性让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A nicety is a fine detail or distinction, especially one that is considered to be important or elegant.

words.ex: He planted carrots in a small patch.
words.ex_cn: 他在一小块地上种了胡萝卜。
words.en: A patch is a piece of material used to mend a hole or a weak spot in something, or a small area that is different from the area around it.

words.ex: He left school at 15, which was too premature.
words.ex_cn: 他15岁就离开了学校，这太早了。
words.en: Happening or done before the usual or expected time; not fully developed or mature.

words.ex: His residence is near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他的住所靠近公园。
words.en: A residence is a house or place where someone lives.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.ex: He felt guilt for his sin of lying.
words.ex_cn: 他因撒谎的罪行感到内疚。
words.en: Sin is an action or behaviour that is considered to be morally wrong according to religious or social laws.

words.ex: She is wearing a black stocking.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着一只黑色长筒袜。
words.en: A stocking is a piece of clothing which fits closely over the foot and is worn up to the knee or higher. Stockings are usually made of nylon or silk and are worn by women.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.ex: The teacher tongue-lashed the student for not doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生没做作业而训斥了他。
words.en: To scold or criticize someone severely.

words.ex: He committed a transgression by stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了过错。
words.en: A transgression is an act that goes against a law, rule, or code of conduct; an offense.

words.tr: adj. 不习惯；不适应；反常的；不一般的
words.ex: He was unaccustomed to the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 他不习惯寒冷的天气。
words.en: If you are unaccustomed to something, you are not used to it and find it strange or difficult.

words.tr: adj. 不劳而获的; 不应得的; 自然得到的; 不相称的
words.ex: He felt guilty about the unearned income he received.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己收到的那些不劳而获的收入感到内疚。
words.en: Unearned income is income derived from sources other than employment, such as dividends, interest, or rent.

chapters.name: Unit 7 PASSAGE Ⅱ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 不习惯于……的；对……不熟悉的
words.ex: She was unaccustomed to the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 她不习惯寒冷的天气。
words.en: To not be used to something or to find something unusual because it is not what you usually experience.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 驱逐；赶出；排斥
words.ex: The village cast out the thief for stealing food.
words.ex_cn: 村庄把小偷驱逐出去了，因为他偷了食物。
words.en: To force someone to leave a place, especially a social group.

words.ex: The farmer shouts to chase away the birds from the field.
words.ex_cn: 农民大声喊叫，把鸟儿从田里赶走。
words.en: To force someone or something to leave or go away, often by pursuing them.

words.tr: phrase. 靠近；拉近关系；逐渐接近
words.ex: As the sun set, the two boats began to draw closer.
words.ex_cn: 随着太阳落山，两艘船开始逐渐靠近。
words.en: To move or cause to move towards a place or person; to approach.

words.tr: 短语动词. 逐渐接近；慢慢靠近
words.ex: The bus draw nearer to the school.
words.ex_cn: 公交车越来越靠近学校。
words.en: To come closer in space or time.

words.tr: phrase. 打扰；侵扰；闯入；干涉
words.ex: Please do not intrude upon my privacy.
words.ex_cn: 请不要侵犯我的隐私。
words.en: If you say that someone is intruding on a particular situation, you mean that they are involving themselves in it in a way that is not welcome or not appropriate.

words.tr: phrase. 打扰；侵扰；闯入；干涉
words.ex: Please do not intrude on my privacy.
words.ex_cn: 请不要侵犯我的隐私。
words.en: To intrude on someone or something means to involve yourself in a situation where you are not wanted or are considered not to belong.

words.tr: phrase. 闯入；侵入；干涉；打扰
words.ex: He does not like people who intrude into his home.
words.ex_cn: 他不喜欢闯入他家的人。
words.en: To enter or be present in a place or situation where one is not wanted or welcome.

words.ex: The lion preys on weak deer.
words.ex_cn: 狮子捕食虚弱的鹿。
words.en: To hunt and kill another animal for food; to exploit or harm someone who is weaker.

chapters.name: Unit 8 Part Two New Words

words.tr:
adj. 古老的；
n. 古董；
words.ex: He bought an antique chair from the old market.
words.ex_cn: 他从旧市场买了一把古老的椅子。
words.en: Something that is antique is old and often valuable because it is rare or well made.

words.ex: The lab tests show biochemical changes in the blood.
words.ex_cn: 实验室检测显示血液中出现了生化变化。
words.en: relating to the chemical processes and substances which occur within living organisms

words.ex: The country is on the brink of war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正处于战争的边缘。
words.en: If you are on the brink of something, you are about to do it or experience it.

words.tr: n. 时间生物学；生物钟学
words.ex: He studies chronobiology to understand sleep patterns.
words.ex_cn: 他研究时间生物学以了解睡眠模式。
words.en: Chronobiology is the study of periodic (cyclic) phenomena in living organisms and their adaptation to solar- and lunar-related rhythms.

words.ex: Some people follow that cult blindly.
words.ex_cn: 有些人盲目追随那个狂热崇拜。
words.en: A cult is a group of people who have extreme admiration for a particular person, idea, or thing, often following unusual or extreme practices or beliefs.

words.ex: The software can desynchronize the system clocks of two computers.
words.ex_cn: 该软件可以使两台计算机的系统时钟去同步。
words.en: To cause something to lose synchronization or to operate at different times or rates.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.tr: adj. 西班牙的；西班牙和葡萄牙的；拉丁美洲的
words.ex: He is a Hispanic student from Spain.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名来自西班牙的西班牙裔学生。
words.en: relating to Spain or to Spanish-speaking countries, especially those of Latin America.

words.ex: Humankind needs to protect the Earth.
words.ex_cn: 人类需要保护地球。
words.en: Humankind refers to all human beings collectively; the human race.

words.ex: The humidity in the room made the air feel heavy.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的湿度让空气感觉很闷。
words.en: Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air. High humidity makes the air feel wet and sticky.

words.tr: adj. 天生的；先天的；天赋的
words.ex: He has an inborn talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 他天生就有音乐才能。
words.en: An inborn quality or ability is one that you have had naturally since birth.

words.ex: The country wants to industrialize quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家想快速工业化。
words.en: To industrialize means to develop industry in a country or region on a wide scale.

words.ex: The internal parts of the machine need repair.
words.ex_cn: 机器的内部零件需要修理。
words.en: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a particular person, object, or place.

words.ex: The mob broke the windows and shouted loudly.
words.ex_cn: 乌合之众砸了窗户并大声喊叫。
words.en: A mob is a large crowd of people, especially one that is disorderly and intent on causing trouble or violence.

words.tr: adj. 外向的；即将离职的；往外去的；
words.ex: He is an outgoing boy who loves talking to new people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的男孩，喜欢和新朋友聊天。
words.en: Someone who is outgoing is very friendly and likes meeting and talking to people.

words.ex: Children develop perceptual skills by playing with toys.
words.ex_cn: 儿童通过玩玩具发展知觉能力。
words.en: Relating to the ability to interpret or become aware of something through the senses.

words.tr: v. 重塑；改造；给…以新形态
words.ex: He wants to reshape his life after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他想在事故后重新塑造自己的生活。
words.en: To reshape something means to change its form or structure, often in order to improve it.

words.ex: The system needs to resynchronize its clocks every day.
words.ex_cn: 系统需要每天重新同步其时钟。
words.en: To synchronize again or anew.

words.ex: The robot cleans the floor every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器人每天打扫地板。
words.en: A robot is a machine that is programmed to move and perform certain tasks automatically.

words.ex: He cooks soup on the stove.
words.ex_cn: 他用炉子煮汤。
words.en: A stove is a piece of equipment which provides heat, either for cooking or for heating a room.

words.ex: We need to synchronise the clocks before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 我们在会议前需要把时钟调同步。
words.en: To synchronise is to cause to occur or operate at the same time or rate.

words.tr: n. [电] 同步装置；同步闪光装置
words.ex: The synchronizer ensures that the images are captured at the same instant.
words.ex_cn: 同步装置确保图像在同一时刻被捕捉。
words.en: A synchronizer is a device or mechanism that ensures two or more processes or devices operate in unison or at the same rate.

words.ex: The two devices need synchronization to work together.
words.ex_cn: 这两个设备需要同步才能一起工作。
words.en: The process of causing things to happen or operate at the same time or rate.

words.ex: He studied hard, thereby passing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，因此通过了考试。
words.en: You use thereby to introduce an important result or consequence of the event or action you have just mentioned.

words.ex: He wears a vintage timepiece on his wrist.
words.ex_cn: 他手腕上戴着一块复古的计时器。
words.en: A timepiece is a device, such as a clock or watch, that measures or indicates time.

words.ex: The people rose up against the tyranny of the king.
words.ex_cn: 人民反抗了国王的暴虐。
words.en: Tyranny is cruel and unfair treatment by someone with power over other people, or a government in which a single ruler has absolute power.

words.ex: The diary helped unlock the mystery of her disappearance.
words.ex_cn: 这本日记帮助揭开了她失踪的谜团。
words.en: To unlock something means to open it, or to make it possible for someone to open it, by turning a key or pushing a button.

words.ex: The team acted in unison to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 团队一致行动赢得了比赛。
words.en: If two or more people do something in unison, they do it together at the same time.

words.ex: He checks the time on his wristwatch.
words.ex_cn: 他看下手表上的时间。
words.en: A wristwatch is a small clock that you wear on a strap around your wrist.

chapters.name: Unit 8 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: He needs to adjust to the new school.
words.ex_cn: 他需要适应新学校。
words.en: If you adjust to a new situation or get used to it, you change your behaviour or ideas so that you can deal with it successfully.

words.ex: He insists on walking to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持每天步行上学。
words.en: If you insist on something, you demand it and refuse to accept any alternative.

words.tr: phrase. 鼓起（勇气、力量等）；唤起（记忆、情感等）
words.ex: She tried to summon up the courage to speak in front of the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 她试图鼓起勇气在众人面前讲话。
words.en: To call upon or bring forth a particular quality or resource within oneself, especially courage or strength.

words.ex: We think of water as a basic need.
words.ex_cn: 我们认为水是一种基本需求。
